newsitem.title: USA: NHL ice hockey-FLYERS ACQUIRE COFFEY FROM WHALERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ice hockey-FLYERS ACQUIRE COFFEY FROM WHALERS.

text.p: The Philadelphia Flyers completed the much-anticipated trade for Paul Coffey on Sunday, acquiring the NHL's all-time leading scorer among defencemen from the Hartford Whalers.
The Flyers sent the Whalers defenceman Kevin Haller and two 1997 draft picks, including a first round selection, in return for the 35-year-old Coffey.
Coffey has not been happy since Hartford acquired him from Detroit in the Brendan Shanahan trade on October 9. Coffey had three goals and five assists in 20 games with the Whalers.
"The last three or four days, the talks heated up," said Philadelphia general manager Bob Clarke.

"It had been discussed on and off for the last couple of months, but over the last few days, Hartford decided that they wanted to trade him, that we were one of the teams they wanted to trade him to."

Coffey provides an offensive presence on the blue line that Philadelphia has not had since Mark Howe was in his prime. He will quarterback a Flyers' power play that has ranked near the bottom of the NHL all season.

Coffey is a three-time Norris Trophy winner as the league's best defenceman. He is eighth on the NHL's all-time scoring list and first among defencemen with 1,418 points. He holds the single-season record for goals by a defenceman with 48 in 1985-86 with the Edmonton Oilers.

He won three Stanley Cups with the Oilers, who traded him to Pittsburgh as part of a seven-player deal in November 1987. He captured another Stanley Cup with the Penguins, who dealt him to Los Angeles in February 1992.
The Flyers also obtained a 1997 third-round draft pick, while shipping first and seventh-round selections to Hartford.
Haller, 26, had five assists in 27 games for Philadelphia.
